name: design-system-workspace
//: Root of the design-system npm workspace. NOT a shippable package — it
declares the members and pins the shared toolchain.
Two members, BOTH published to GitHub Packages:
There is exactly ONE way anything here reaches a consumer: publish a
version. No path dependency, no symlink into a consumer's tree, ever — that
gives one package two simultaneous truths, and the two drift the moment
tokens is published rather than private because it no longer shares a
workspace with its consumers; the registry is the only way across.
The member list is EXPLICIT and must stay that way — never `packages/*`.
Adding a member silently gives it a symlink to the other's source, which
is how a broken package passes CI here and only breaks after publishing.

//scripts: Script commentary lives HERE, beside `scripts`, and never inside it.
npm tolerates `//name` comment keys among the scripts themselves.
Storybook does not: its build walks the `scripts` object calling `.match()`
on every value, so an array-valued comment key crashes it with
`TypeError: s?.match is not a function` — from `computeStorybookMetadata`,
naming neither package.json nor the key, and not skippable with
Keeping the comments as arrays (readable, multi-line) but moving them out
of `scripts` costs only adjacency, and this object sits immediately above

The generator renders tokens.json into this repo's outputs and NOTHING
outside it. An output that writes into a consumer's tree would encode one
reader's directory layout into a published package.
lint: Fans out per member rather than running ESLint once from the root, and
there is deliberately NO `eslint.config.js` at the repo root — the rules
live in `eslint.base.js`, which each member re-exports. ESLint discovers
a flat config by walking UP from its cwd, so a root one is also found by
any subdirectory with its own ESLint setup. Read eslint.base.js before
ci: The whole local gate: token drift, format, lint, typecheck, test.
Mirrors what .github/workflows/pr.yml runs, so `npm run ci` green
locally is a fair predictor of a green PR. It does NOT build the
workbench — CI does that separately, because it is slower than the rest
of the gate put together and breaks far less often.
skills:check: Gates every SKILL.md in the repo — the shipped plugin's and the
contributor-only ones under .claude/skills alike. Cheap and dependency-
free, so it sits early in `ci` beside the other fast checks.
scripts/check-skills.ts owns the reasoning, including why a description
must declare its audience: the skills CLI walks the WHOLE repo, so a
consumer installing with a wildcard would otherwise pull in skills about
typecheck:scripts: The fifth typecheck program — scripts/. See tsconfig.scripts.json for why
it is its own program rather than part of the workbench's.
typecheck:workbench: The fourth typecheck program — the stories, which until 0.8.3 no program
covered. tsconfig.workbench.json has the full reasoning, including why one
program can hold both leaves and why `react-native` resolves to the real
package's types rather than to workbench/react-native.ts.
This is not hypothetical tidiness: the Button story shipped
`intent="danger"`, an intent that does not exist, and rendered an unstyled
button under that label until this program was added. Neither the axe gate
nor `storybook:build` can see a wrong prop NAME — the first checks the
accessibility tree, the second only transpiles.
test:workbench: A plain-Node Vitest project (see the `workbench` project in
project so this stays cheap. Runs workbench/story-coverage.test.ts, which
asserts every component under packages/design-system/src/ has a matching
"a story is one directory away from its component, so a new component can
be added without one." Placed in `ci` before `test:a11y` on purpose — a
missing story is cheap to detect and should fail before the expensive
browser suite runs, same ordering logic as pr.yml's version-bump gate.
test:coverage: The story suite with V8 coverage over packages/*/src (config in
vitest.config.ts, which also says why this is not part of `ci`). The
same report backs the Coverage toggle in Storybook's testing widget.
storybook: The component workbench: the only place a component is LOOKED AT rather
than asserted about. `storybook` is the dev loop (./scripts/dev-up.sh
wraps it); `storybook:build` produces the static site CI builds to prove
the workbench still compiles. Read .storybook/main.ts before changing
either — it explains why the React Native Web framework renders BOTH
leaves, and workbench/react-native.ts explains the one export it

scripts.ci: npm run tokens:check && npm run skills:check && npm run format && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run typecheck:workbench && npm run typecheck:scripts && npm run test && npm run test:workbench && npm run test:a11y

//devDependencies: ESLint/Prettier/TypeScript are pinned deliberately: these packages are
linted and typechecked HERE but compiled by the CONSUMER, since both
publish source. Options stricter here than a consumer's are safe; looser
ones ship errors downstream. TypeScript is 5.9 rather than the 7.x line —
`erasableSyntaxOnly` (5.8+) is the feature this workspace depends on.
